text: Burden scales can structure assessment: the 2024 meta-analysis identified the ZBI as the most used measure, and the 2025 predictor review also found it used more often than the other listed scales. Scores should be interpreted alongside the caregiver’s own account because validated measures may miss aspects of lived experience. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: A 2025 review of forty-one studies identified the impact of motor symptoms on daily activities and severity of neuropsychiatric symptoms as burden predictors, but found evidence inconclusive for disease stage, duration and motor symptom severity; stage or duration alone should therefore not be used as a universal burden rule. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: A Parkinson’s News Today feature describes irritability, exhaustion and low patience as burnout warning signs and illustrates the value one care partner places on specific offers of practical help. This is a reported personal experience and support guidance, not a validated diagnostic rule or causal trial. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Reviews differ on disease duration and severity: a 2024 review reported higher burden with longer duration and greater severity, whereas Lesley and colleagues’ 2025 predictor review judged disease duration, stage and motor severity inconclusive. These should not be presented as universal independent predictors. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: The evidence base underrepresents some care partners: the 2025 review calls for younger and non-spousal caregivers and more diverse samples, while its limitations describe predominantly older female spouses and recruitment biased toward outpatient settings. Generalization to all caregiver relationships and disease stages requires caution. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: A patient-education RCT involving 46 care partners found short-term improvements in psychosocial problems and need for help after eight weekly sessions. A separate formative evaluation found improvements in those domains but none on health-state, quality-of-life or depression measures; outcomes should be reported by domain rather than as a blanket improvement in well-being. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Evidence on cognition requires qualification: the scoping review described cognitive impairment as a consistent burden predictor, while the 2025 review restricted to multivariable analyses found general cognitive function did not predict burden. These differently scoped findings should remain attributed rather than collapsed into a universal cognitive-score rule. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Caregiver burden describes adverse effects on caregivers’ physical, emotional, social and financial well-being; it should be assessed as the care partner’s own experience rather than equated with the person with PD being a burden. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Poorer caregiver mental health and greater patient neuropsychiatric symptom severity are associated with greater burden. The 2025 predictor review also identified the impact of motor symptoms on daily living, rather than motor symptoms alone, as a consistent predictor. These observational findings do not establish causality. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Practical support should address the care partner’s own unmet needs, including psychosocial help and opportunities for respite; these are support priorities described in the literature, rather than a guarantee that any particular service will reduce burden. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Care partner burden in PD encompasses effects on emotional and physical health, social participation and finances; caregiving can also be rewarding, so burden should not be assumed to define every relationship. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Caregiver mental health warrants assessment in its own right: a cross-sectional baseline analysis of 175 patient-caregiver pairs associated caregiver depression and anxiety with burden, and a 2025 systematic review identified poorer caregiver mental health among predictors. These are associations, not proof that treating anxiety alone reduces burden. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: In interviews with 36 care partners across 11 European countries, participants described information needs distinct from those of the person with PD, especially medication management, side effects, contacts for problems and responses to behavioural or mental health symptoms. These qualitative findings describe needs, not intervention effectiveness. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Practical support options include planned time away from caregiving, help from relatives or friends, social-work resource navigation and respite or in-home assistance; the Foundation recommends these options, and qualitative research documents care partners’ unmet need for time to themselves. This supports a needs-based support plan, without establishing a quantified treatment effect. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Peer groups need a suitable format: the European interview study found mixed experiences, including reluctance to voice concerns in front of the person with PD; participants appreciated care-partner-specific groups. Generic support groups should not be assumed to meet everyone’s needs. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: A small preliminary randomised trial enrolled 30 distressed care partners and compared 12–14 CBT sessions with no treatment; it reported greater improvement in psychological distress, strain and subjective burden, maintained over a further three-month follow-up. The authors called for larger studies and longer-term assessment. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: CBT evidence for care-partner burden is mixed: the preliminary Secker–Brown trial reported improvement, whereas a 2024 meta-analysis reported no significant pooled burden reduction. The positive small trial does not establish a reliable general effect, and the pooled null result does not prove that no individual can benefit. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: The Parkinson’s Foundation care-partner page directs readers to its Helpline, local chapters, support groups and free self-paced care-partner courses. These are resource-navigation options; the page is not trial evidence for reducing burden. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Care partnering includes emotional support as well as physical tasks, and the role changes as PD progresses; support planning should recognize this evolving involvement. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: In the PEPP randomized trial, sixty-four people with PD and 46 caregivers were allocated to education or usual care. Eight weekly 90-minute sessions improved caregivers’ psychosocial problems and need for help at assessment one week after completion; this short follow-up does not establish durable benefit. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: A survey of 141 current and 15 former PD carers identified unmet needs around finding balance, relationship changes, and coping with reduced emotions and motivation. About half of current carers were interested in exchanging experience with former carers, and commonality with peers mattered. This was a needs-and-preferences study, not a trial proving burden reduction. (low confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

text: Psychoeducation and other caregiver support interventions are promising, but reliable long-term burden reduction is not established across programs. The scoping review identified small samples, inconsistent outcomes and limited longitudinal data; the 2024 meta-analysis found no significant pooled caregiver-burden effect for cognitive behavior therapy. Improvement in mood or coping should not be described automatically as improvement in burden. (medium confidence)
keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD
